entities.name: Academy Museum of Motion Pictures
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles is the world's largest museum dedicated to the history and science of filmmaking, opened in 2021 after a $388 million renovation of the former May Company building. Created by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences — the organization that presents the Oscars — it houses over 13 million objects in the world's most comprehensive film archive.

The museum's design by Italian architect Renzo Piano added a new spherical glass structure containing the 1,000-seat David Geffen Theater and the Dolby Family Terrace, connected to the 1939 Streamline Moderne building by glass bridges. The opening exhibition, 'Stories of Cinema,' presented 200 years of cinematic history through artifacts including Dorothy's ruby slippers from The Wizard of Oz, Rosebud from Citizen Kane, and Darth Vader's helmet from Star Wars.

The museum opened to controversy over its representation of marginalized communities: the original opening exhibition was criticized for underrepresenting Black filmmakers, Japanese-American cinema, and other non-Western traditions. The 'Backdrop' exhibition on the history of racist portrayals in Hollywood, and dedicated programs on Japanese-American cinema and Latin representation, reflected reckonings with Hollywood's complex racial history. Annual Oscar screenings and education programs make it the educational hub of the global film industry.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Academy Museum is the world's most comprehensive film archive, created by Hollywood's own institution to grapple with cinema's century of both artistic achievement and racial representation failures.
